A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PyPop7 library. All five pages of v1 and seven pages of v2 are readable and support comparison; both end with references and contain no appendices.

before.justification: v1 provides LMMAES usage code for the Rosenbrock function but reports no execution output or original empirical findings. Mentioned repeatability reports are not included.

after.justification: v2 retains a code-only demonstration without experimental outcomes. It mentions repeatability reports and use in an earlier publication, but does not reproduce empirical results.

M1.justification: The reported optimizer repertoire expands from >60 variants across 12 families in v1 Section 2 to >72 across 13 in v2 Section 3, explicitly adding Bayesian optimization. This extends the library's available algorithm components while retaining the unified framework and demonstrated LMMAES procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions illustrate use with the same 1,000-dimensional Rosenbrock problem. Neither reports evaluated datasets or additional test scenarios; the expanded discussion of applications does not establish actual evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version reports an evaluated baseline comparison. DEAP, PyBrain, and PaGMO are newly discussed in v2's related work, but are not experimentally compared with PyPop7.

E3.justification: The illustrative LMMAES settings remain unchanged: 1,000 dimensions, bounds [-5, 5], a 3,600-second runtime limit, fitness threshold 1e-10, initial mean 4, and initial step size 0.3. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Neither PDF contains ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity analyses, error analyses, or empirical case studies. The retained usage example demonstrates an interface without analyzing outcomes.

E5.justification: Both repeatability subsections require explicit random seeds, and both examples set seed_rng to 0. Neither reports repeated-run counts, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests; v2's expanded repeatability discussion adds no statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Neither version reports numerical outputs, measured performance comparisons, rankings, or qualitative experimental findings. The changed optimizer counts describe library capabilities rather than empirical results.

T1.justification: v2 expands discussion and citations concerning algorithm theory and techniques for addressing dimensionality, but introduces no formal definitions, assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations. Replacing the inline Rosenbrock implementation with an import does not establish a mathematical change.

C1.justification: The abstract expands claimed library coverage from >60 variants and 12 families to >72 and 13. The introduction also makes research repeatability an explicit design objective. The central contribution remains a unified open-source library supporting large-scale BBO benchmarking and applications.

C2.justification: v1's page 2 footnote excludes research relying on partial additive separability because of its perceived limited practical applicability; v2 removes that scope qualification. v2 also explicitly discusses the tradeoff between requiring few prior assumptions and slow convergence.

D1.justification: v2 Section 3.1 adds Scikit-Learn to the stated dependencies and discloses occasional Numba acceleration. The example now imports Rosenbrock from the library, and new text points to COCO/NeverGrad integration tutorials and a companion applications website. The main code and documentation destinations are retained.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning beyond v1's COCO/NeverGrad discussion, adding comparisons with DEAP, PyBrain, and PaGMO and explaining their differing purposes or coverage. It also broadens the algorithm-theory literature and claims early provision of repeatability reports spanning many optimizers. These additions substantively develop the library's relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, related work becomes a separate expanded section, and the framework overview gains a reorganized taxonomy and theoretical context. v2 also expands explanatory prose and adds keywords, revised author information, and funding acknowledgments.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted, including typography, the title and author block, running headers, page numbering, bibliography presentation, and the code listing's size and styling. Neither version contains experimental figures or tables.

improvement.justification: v2's expanded comparisons with other libraries and additional implementation disclosures make PyPop7's role and practical use easier to assess. These provide a modest improvement in informativeness, partly offset by removing v1's explicit separability-related scope boundary. The broader capability claims are not accompanied by empirical validation, so they do not establish improved optimizer performance.
